statements.text: All ten tested sequences from IS3 ends gained de-novo promoter activity through single point mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All 10 sequences could evolve de-novo promoter activity from single point mutations.
statements.note: The abstract states all 10 sequences evolved promoter activity from single point mutations.

statements.text: IS3 ends contain roughly half as many proto-promoter sequences as the rest of the E. coli genome.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The ends of IS3s harbor ~1.5 times as many such proto-promoter sequences than the E. coli genome.
statements.note: The abstract reports IS3 ends have about 1.5 times as many proto-promoters, not fewer.

statements.text: The new promoters measurably raised expression of genes next to IS3 insertions in living cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our observations can help to explain why mobile DNA may persist in prokaryotic genomes.
statements.note: Promoter activity was measured in a reporter assay; expression of adjacent host genes in vivo was not tested.

statements.text: At least 26% of the 706 characterized IS3 elements were estimated to already encode promoters.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We also estimate that at least 26% of the 706 characterized IS3s already encode promoters.
statements.note: The abstract gives this exact estimate of pre-existing promoters among characterized IS3s.

statements.text: Retrotransposable elements and endogenous retroviruses make up roughly 45% of the human genome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RTEs and ERVs are mobile genetic elements that constitute about 45% of our genome.
statements.note: The abstract states these elements make up about 45% of the genome.

statements.text: Blocking LINE-1 replication with reverse transcriptase inhibitors prevented neuronal death in the transgenic mice.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Together, these findings support the hypothesis that TDP-43 pathology triggers RTE/ERV expression in the motor cortex, that such expression marks cells for programmed cell death, with non-cell autonomous effects on nearby neurons and glial cells.
statements.note: No intervention blocking retrotransposons was tested; the study is observational on this point.

statements.text: RTE and ERV expression appeared earlier in the mutant hTDP-43-Q331K mice than in wild-type TDP-43 mice.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This expression begins at the age of onset of neurological phenotypes, earlier in the hTDP-43-Q331K animals and much later in hTDP-43-WT.
statements.note: The abstract reports earlier onset of expression in Q331K animals than in wild-type.

statements.text: The LINE-1-EGFP labeled neurons survived and persisted over time rather than dying.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: These EGFP-labeled neurons undergo cell death and are therefore lost over time.
statements.note: The abstract says the labeled neurons undergo cell death and are lost, the opposite of surviving.

statements.text: ChAHP2 is directed mainly to SINE retrotransposons rather than to ERVs and LINEs.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ChAHP2 is predominantly targeted to endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) and long interspersed elements (LINEs) via HP1β-mediated binding of H3K9 trimethylated histones.
statements.note: The abstract says ChAHP2 targets ERVs and LINEs, not SINEs.

statements.text: In ChAHP2 the subunit ADNP found in ChAHP is swapped out for ADNP2.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here we identify ChAHP2, a protein complex homologous to ChAHP, in which ADNP is replaced by ADNP2.
statements.note: The abstract defines ChAHP2 as ChAHP with ADNP replaced by ADNP2.

statements.text: Mutations in ADNP2 cause a human neurodevelopmental disorder like the one caused by ADNP.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Together, our results reveal that the ChAHP and ChAHP2 complexes function to control both nonautonomous and autonomous retrotransposons by complementary activities, further adding to the complexity of mammalian transposon control.
statements.note: The abstract concerns molecular function in retrotransposon control, not human disease phenotypes.

statements.text: Deleting ADNP2 relieves repression of ERVs and LINE1, an effect worsened by also depleting ADNP.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Genetic ablation of ADNP2 alleviates ERV and LINE1 repression, which is synthetically exacerbated by additional depletion of ADNP.
statements.note: The abstract reports this synthetic exacerbation when both ADNP2 and ADNP are lost.

statements.text: Before clinical relapse, ctDNA was detected in 97% of the non-pCR TNBC patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA was detected in 97% of patients before clinical relapse.
statements.note: The abstract gives a 97% pre-relapse detection rate.

statements.text: Capecitabine lengthened overall survival compared with a no-adjuvant-treatment control arm in this cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In these cases, adjuvant chemotherapy with capecitabine improves disease-free survival in ∼15% of patients.
statements.note: A disease-free-survival figure is cited as background; no overall-survival comparison against an untreated arm is reported here.

statements.text: Detection of ctDNA at the post-NAC pre-operative T1 time point was linked to 95% distant-disease relapse-free survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We confirmed that the lack of detection of ctDNA at the post-NAC pre-operative (T1) time point is highly prognostic, with 95% distant-disease relapse free survival.
statements.note: It was the lack of ctDNA detection at T1, not detection, that signalled 95% relapse-free survival.

statements.text: Capecitabine treatment coincided with ctDNA clearance in 41% of cases, and that clearance signalled good prognosis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: capecitabine treatment was associated with clearance of ctDNA in 41% of cases, and clearance (from detection to non-detection) was associated with good prognosis.
statements.note: The abstract reports 41% clearance and its association with good prognosis.

statements.text: The analysis found 131 EAC-specific and 49 ESCC-specific differentially expressed genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 131 genes were identified as EAC-specific DEGs, whereas 49 genes were recognized as ESCC-specific DEGs.
statements.note: The abstract gives these exact subtype-specific DEG counts.

statements.text: A six-gene prognostic risk model (RHOV, SYTL1, MT1X, PRRG4, KCNK5, CCL20) was built for EAC.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: For EAC, a prognostic risk model was constructed, including RHOV, SYTL1, MT1X, PRRG4, KCNK5, and CCL20
statements.note: The abstract lists exactly these six genes in the EAC risk model.

statements.text: TUSC3 expression predicted response to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in ESCC patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In ESCC, TUSC3 was identified as a prognostic biomarker and was validated in tissue samples.
statements.note: TUSC3 was reported as a prognostic biomarker; prediction of treatment response was not tested.

statements.text: EAC, not ESCC, showed significant enrichment of extracellular matrix, cell cycle, EMT, and hypoxia pathways.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of the extracellular matrix (ECM)-related pathway, along with the cell cycle, epithelial‒mesenchymal transition (EMT), and hypoxia signaling pathways, in ESCC.
statements.note: These pathways were enriched in ESCC, not EAC.

statements.text: Patients with MAF above 5% at any time point had a better prognosis than those with MAF below 5%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: patients with MAF > 5% any time point had a significantly poorer prognosis compared with patients with MAF < 5%
statements.note: Higher MAF was linked to poorer, not better, prognosis.

statements.text: No detectable ctDNA at baseline before first-line therapy was associated with better overall and progression-free survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Absence of detectable ctDNA in baseline samples prior to first-line therapy was associated with improved OS (HR = 0.13; P = 0.02) and progression-free survival (PFS; HR = 0.31; P = 0.008).
statements.note: The abstract ties absent baseline ctDNA to improved OS and PFS.

statements.text: Patients with MAF above 5% had far shorter median overall survival than those below 5% (4 vs 21 months).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: median OS 4 months vs. 21 months, P < 0.001
statements.note: The abstract reports median OS of 4 versus 21 months by MAF cutoff.

statements.text: The assay also detected BAP1 mutations, which further stratified patient prognosis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: using an IVDR-certified digital PCR assay targeting GNAQQ209 and GNA11Q209 mutations.
statements.note: The assay targeted only GNAQ and GNA11 Q209 mutations; BAP1 is not mentioned.

statements.text: The platform was evaluated in 30 leiomyosarcoma patients treated with durvalumab plus either olaparib or cediranib.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 30 LMS patients treated with durvalumab plus olaparib or cediranib
statements.note: The abstract states the cohort was 30 LMS patients on these regimens.

statements.text: Signatures of B-cell and T-cell activation were significantly associated with shorter progression-free survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Signatures reflecting B-cell activation, T-cell activation, and extracellular matrix organization were significantly associated with improved progression-free survival
statements.note: These immune signatures were tied to improved, not shorter, PFS.

statements.text: cfDNA active-chromatin profiling predicted overall survival better than standard RECIST imaging in these patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: cfDNA ac profiling represents a promising non-invasive strategy to predict clinical benefit from CPI-based therapy in LMS.
statements.note: The abstract frames the method as predicting clinical benefit; no head-to-head comparison with RECIST imaging for survival is reported.

statements.text: Patients with clinical benefit showed enrichment of cell death, interferon-γ signaling, and immune activation pathways.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients achieving CBR demonstrated enrichment of pathways related to cell death, interferon-γ signaling, and immune activation.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly these enriched pathways in patients achieving clinical benefit.

statements.text: TE-lncRNAs made up 40.4% of all lncRNAs, with 2119 of them identified.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: constitute 2119 TE-lncRNAs (40.4% of all lncRNAs)
statements.note: The abstract reports 2119 TE-lncRNAs, 40.4% of all lncRNAs.

statements.text: TE-lncRNAs were shown to be required for S2 cell survival under heavy metal stress.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The regulatory network of a key transcription factor was rewired by transposons, potentially recruiting other transcription factors to exert regulatory functions under heavy metal stress.
statements.note: Regulatory associations were described, but no knockout or survival experiment establishing a requirement was done.

statements.text: The LTR/Gypsy family was the most frequent type of transposon insertion found.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The LTR/Gypsy family was the most common transposon insertion.
statements.note: The abstract names LTR/Gypsy as the most common inserted transposon.

statements.text: Compared with other lncRNAs, TE-lncRNAs were shorter and more highly conserved.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Compared with lncRNAs, TE-lncRNAs showed longer lengths, a lower conservation, and lower levels but a higher specificity of expression.
statements.note: TE-lncRNAs were longer and less conserved, not shorter and more conserved.

statements.text: The expanded, variable pepper genome sizes were attributed to whole-genome duplication rather than transposable element accumulation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The expanded and variable genome sizes were attributed to differential transposable element accumulations, which shaped 3D chromatin architecture
statements.note: Genome-size variation was attributed to transposable element accumulation, not whole-genome duplication.

statements.text: Variable pepper genome sizes were attributed to differences in transposable element accumulation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The expanded and variable genome sizes were attributed to differential transposable element accumulations
statements.note: The abstract directly attributes genome-size variation to differential TE accumulation.

statements.text: The study assembled 11 Capsicum genomes, two of them gap-free, spanning four wild and all five domesticated species.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here we present 11 high-quality Capsicum genome assemblies, including two gap-free genomes, covering four wild and all five domesticated pepper species.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly these assemblies and species coverage.

statements.text: The newly bred pepper lines produced higher yields in field trials.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings on the genomic and functional evolution of Capsicum will benefit pepper breeding.
statements.note: Breeding benefit is stated as a prospect; no field-trial yield result is reported.

statements.text: Of the 165 patients studied, 35 (21.2%) experienced a relapse.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: One hundred sixty-five patients were included in this study, with 35 (21.2%) relapses.
statements.note: The abstract gives 165 patients and 35 (21.2%) relapses.

statements.text: At the landmark time point, positive MRD was associated with longer disease-free survival than negative MRD.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: At landmark, positive MRD was associated with shorter disease-free survival (DFS) than negative MRD
statements.note: Positive MRD was linked to shorter, not longer, disease-free survival.

statements.text: The 769-gene panel detected MRD a median of six months before radiographic imaging.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: MRD detection was conducted using the MinerVa platform (Genecast Precision Diagnostic Co., Ltd. Wuhan, China) using a tumor-informed strategy based on a fixed next-generation sequencing panel spanning 769 cancer-related genes.
statements.note: The panel size is given, but no lead-time figure relative to imaging is reported.

statements.text: ctDNA clearance during adjuvant therapy was associated with a better prognosis than persistently detectable ctDNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Clearance of ctDNA during AT was associated with a better prognosis than persistently detected ctDNA ( P < .001).
statements.note: The abstract ties ctDNA clearance to better prognosis.

statements.text: Among proofreading-deficient TCGA tumors, somatic variants occurred mainly in endometrial cancers (75%).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Somatic variants occurred mainly in endometrial cancers (75% of proofreading-deficient TCGA cancers)
statements.note: The abstract reports 75% of proofreading-deficient TCGA cancers were endometrial.

statements.text: POLE-mutant tumors responded better to immune checkpoint inhibitors than POLD1-mutant tumors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Despite shared mutational features that make these tumors highly immunogenic, molecular and clinical distinctions between POLE and POLD1 mutations and between somatic and germline variants remain incompletely understood.
statements.note: The tumors are called immunogenic, but checkpoint-inhibitor response was not compared between the two.

statements.text: All germline and somatic pathogenic variants had high AlphaMissense scores and clustered within or near Exo motifs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All germline and somatic PVs had high AlphaMissense scores (0.87-1) and clustered within or near Exo motifs.
statements.note: The abstract reports high AlphaMissense scores and Exo-motif clustering for all PVs.

statements.text: Unlike POLD1, POLE exonuclease-domain variants exhibited haplosufficiency and typically needed a somatic second hit to drive hypermutation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Unlike POLE, POLD1 ED PVs exhibited haplosufficiency, typically requiring a somatic second hit (eg, loss of heterozygosity) or MMR deficiency to drive hypermutation.
statements.note: It was POLD1, not POLE, that showed haplosufficiency requiring a second hit.

statements.text: PRNRP was enriched in proximal tubule cells, while KRAS-mutant PRCC was enriched in distal nephron components.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: RNA-based deconvolution analysis revealed that PRNRP had enrichment in distal nephron components, whereas KRAS -mutant PRCC was enriched in proximal tubule cells ( p = 0.02).
statements.note: The enrichments are reversed: PRNRP was distal-nephron and KRAS-mutant PRCC proximal-tubule.

statements.text: L1CAM immunohistochemistry was positive in PRNRP but negative in KRAS-mutant PRCC.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: IHC staining of L1CAM was positive in PRNRP but negative in KRAS -mutant PRCC
statements.note: The abstract reports this exact L1CAM staining pattern.

statements.text: KRAS-mutant RCC patients responded to KRAS G12C inhibitor therapy in this study.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This contrasts with the genomic complexity and aggressive clinical behavior observed in KRAS -mutant PRCC and URCC, highlighting the need for subtype-specific diagnostic criteria and therapeutic strategies.
statements.note: Therapeutic strategies are called for, but no KRAS-inhibitor treatment response was tested.

statements.text: Seven of the 17 patients (41%) had metastatic disease, and none of them were PRNRP.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Seven patients (41%) had metastatic disease; none were PRNRP.
statements.note: The abstract reports 41% metastatic disease with no PRNRP cases among them.

statements.text: Long-read sequencing traced the ichabod phenotype to a CMC-EnSpm transposon inserted in the ctnnb2 3'UTR.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we discovered that the ich phenotype stems from the insertion of a non-autonomous CMC-Enhancer/Suppressor-mutator (CMC-EnSpm) transposon in the 3'UTR of the gene.
statements.note: The abstract attributes the ich phenotype to this transposon insertion in the 3'UTR.

statements.text: The transposon insertion sharply reduced ctnnb2 transcript stability, which is otherwise very high in early development.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: while wild type ctnnb2 mRNAs exhibit remarkably high stability throughout the early stages of development, the insertion of the transposon dramatically reduces transcript stability.
statements.note: The abstract contrasts high wild-type stability with the sharp reduction caused by the insertion.

statements.text: Inserting the transposon increased the stability of the ctnnb2 transcript during early development.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the insertion of the transposon dramatically reduces transcript stability.
statements.note: The insertion reduced, not increased, transcript stability.

statements.text: Removing the transposon by genome editing rescued the ventralized embryo phenotype.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our findings not only resolve the molecular basis of the ich mutation but also highlight the continuing mutagenic potential of endogenous transposons and reveal unexpected aspects of maternal transcript regulation during early zebrafish development.
statements.note: The molecular cause was resolved, but no transposon-excision rescue experiment is reported.

statements.text: TUSV-int deconvolves the variant types using a deep neural network rather than integer linear programming.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Using integer linear programming (ILP), we deconvolve heterogeneous variant types and resolve them into a clonal lineage tree.
statements.note: The method uses integer linear programming, not a deep neural network.

statements.text: TUSV-int combines bulk DNA-seq with scRNA-seq and jointly handles SNVs, copy-number alterations, and structural variants.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We present TUSV-int, integrating bulk DNA-seq and scRNA-seq into a single deconvolution and phylogenetic inference framework while accommodating single nucleotide variants (SNV), copy number alterations (CNA), and structural variants (SV).
statements.note: The abstract describes exactly this integration and variant coverage.

statements.text: The improved clonal resolution translated into more accurate prediction of patient survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We further demonstrate its ability to better resolve clonal structure and mutational histories on a published DNA-seq/scRNA-seq breast cancer dataset.
statements.note: The method improved clonal resolution, but survival prediction was not evaluated.

statements.text: TUSV-int outperformed methods that lacked scRNA-seq or used a narrower set of variant types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrate improved deconvolution performance over methods lacking scRNA-seq or using more limited variant types.
statements.note: The abstract reports improved performance over those comparator methods.

statements.text: Tumor DNA-assay alterations were detected in 65 of the resected tumors, versus only 4 found only on the RNA assay.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Alterations were detected on the DNA assay for 65 tumors and only on the RNA assay for 4 tumors.
statements.note: The abstract gives 65 DNA-assay and 4 RNA-only tumors.

statements.text: Plasma amplicon sequencing detected recurrence earlier than CT imaging in these patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We assessed the association between circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) identified using amplicon sequencing and evidence of recurrence on CT surveillance.
statements.note: The study assessed association with imaging recurrence, not whether ctDNA preceded imaging.

statements.text: None of the patients with imaging recurrence had detectable ctDNA at the 12-month follow-up.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Four of those 29 patients had evidence of recurrence on imaging, of whom two had biopsy confirmation of recurrence and detectable ctDNA at the 12-month follow-up.
statements.note: Two of the patients with imaging recurrence did have detectable ctDNA at 12 months.

statements.text: The study concluded invasive tissue diagnosis may be avoidable when ctDNA confirms imaging-suspected recurrence.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Invasive tissue diagnosis may be avoidable in patients with ctDNA confirmation of recurrence that is suspected based on imaging.
statements.note: This is stated directly in the abstract's conclusions.

statements.text: The patient-specific panels targeted on average 144 variants per patient.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patient-specific panels were designed targeting an average of 144 variants per patient.
statements.note: The abstract gives an average of 144 variants per patient-specific panel.

statements.text: The assay had a variant-level limit of detection (LOD95) of 12%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: a variant-level limit of detection (LOD95) of 0.12%.
statements.note: The reported LOD95 was 0.12%, not 12%.

statements.text: Tumor-informed variants were found in 26 of 28 patients and de novo variants in 25 of 28.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Tumor-informed variants were detected in 26/28 patients, and de novo variants were observed in 25/28 patients.
statements.note: The abstract gives these exact detection counts.

statements.text: Patients whose ctDNA cleared during vaccination had significantly longer overall survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Longitudinal ctDNA data provided key insights into patients’ responses to vaccine treatment.
statements.note: ctDNA tracked treatment response, but no overall-survival comparison tied to clearance is reported.

statements.text: Bevacizumab plus high-dose furmonertinib roughly doubled median overall survival versus monotherapy (15.31 vs 7.10 months).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: median OS: 15.31 vs 7.10 months, respectively, 95% CI: 0.29-0.82, p = 0.002
statements.note: The abstract reports median OS of 15.31 versus 7.10 months favoring the combination.

statements.text: Furmonertinib monotherapy produced a longer median intracranial PFS than the bevacizumab-plus-furmonertinib combination.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: median iPFS: 6.77 vs 4.04 months, respectively, 95% CI: 0.41-0.98, p = 0.038
statements.note: The combination gave longer iPFS (6.77 months) than monotherapy (4.04 months).

statements.text: Adding bevacizumab raised the rate of serious bleeding adverse events compared with monotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This combination therapy represents a promising strategy for the treatment of a population with unmet needs.
statements.note: Efficacy outcomes are reported, but no bleeding or adverse-event rates are given.

statements.text: Among evaluable patients, 31 of 47 (66%) achieved a CSF ctDNA molecular response.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 31/47 patients (66%) achieved a molecular response
statements.note: The abstract reports 31 of 47 (66%) achieving a molecular response.

statements.text: More than 40% of human C2H2 zinc-finger proteins were significantly enriched at long-range interaction anchors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we find that >40% of human C2H2-ZFPs are significantly enriched at LRI anchors.
statements.note: The abstract reports >40% enrichment at LRI anchors.

statements.text: Disrupting these C2H2-ZFP interactions drove tumor formation in mouse models.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Depletion of a subset of such C2H2-ZFPs is associated with altered expression of genes linked by the LRIs they occupy.
statements.note: Depletion altered gene expression, but no in vivo tumorigenesis experiment is reported.

statements.text: About 35% of LRI-associated C2H2-ZFP binding sites overlapped somatic mutations in cancer genomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ∼35% of LRI-associated C2H2-ZFP binding sites overlap somatic mutations in cancer genomes.
statements.note: The abstract gives roughly 35% overlap with cancer somatic mutations.

statements.text: Interacting C2H2-ZFP pairs were depleted at long-range interactions and rarely shared loop anchors.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: interacting C2H2-ZFP pairs are significantly co-enriched at LRIs and frequently localize to the same or opposing loop anchors.
statements.note: Interacting pairs were co-enriched at LRIs and often shared anchors, the opposite of depleted.

statements.text: In simulated population screening, the ctDNA assay performed worse than low-dose CT.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: in simulated population screenings, our ctDNA assay outperformed both LDCT and a previously established method.
statements.note: The assay outperformed LDCT in the simulations, not the reverse.

statements.text: The model's AUC was about 95.6% in training and 95.7% in validation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 95.59% for the training cohort and 95.74% for the validation cohort.
statements.note: The abstract reports these two AUC values.

statements.text: The model also distinguished lung cancer from other cancer types.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We developed a blood-based multi-omics model using whole-genome cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features to distinguish lung cancer from non-cancer individuals.
statements.note: The model separated lung cancer from non-cancer controls; discrimination from other cancers was not tested.

statements.text: In the external validation cohort the model reached 85.9% sensitivity and 94.78% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with 85.9% sensitivity and 94.78% specificity.
statements.note: The abstract gives these external-validation performance figures.

statements.text: Across the 1000-patient cohort, median cfDNA concentration was 6.25 ng/mL.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: CfDNA concentration varied broadly (median 6.25 ng/mL; range 0.5-1132.9).
statements.note: The abstract reports a median cfDNA concentration of 6.25 ng/mL.

statements.text: Liver and bile duct cancers had higher median cfDNA than other primary sites (13.5 vs 6.1 ng/mL).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: liver/bile duct cancers having higher cfDNA than other sites (median 13.5 vs 6.1 ng/mL, p<0.0001).
statements.note: The abstract gives these median cfDNA values by primary site.

statements.text: Higher cfDNA concentration independently predicted longer progression-free and disease-specific survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfDNA concentration was an independent predictor of shorter PFS (p=0.001) and DSS (p<0.0001)
statements.note: Higher cfDNA predicted shorter, not longer, PFS and disease-specific survival.

statements.text: cfDNA concentration specifically predicted response to immunotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: cfDNA concentration may eventually augment patient selection for aggressive versus palliative interventions, especially in advanced disease.
statements.note: Treatment-selection potential is suggested, but no immunotherapy-response result is reported.

statements.text: The mutational-signature correlation with the BRCA1 germline variant appeared in the breast tumor but not the ovarian tumor.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our findings revealed a correlation between somatic mutational signatures and the BRCA1 germline mutation in the proband with ovarian cancer, while no such association was observed in the tumor tissue from the patient with breast cancer.
statements.note: The correlation was seen in the ovarian tumor, not the breast tumor.

statements.text: A novel BRCA1 germline variant, Phe1695Val, was identified by whole-exome sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A novel germline mutation (Phe1695Val) in BRCA1 was identified through whole-exome sequencing.
statements.note: The abstract reports finding this novel BRCA1 variant by whole-exome sequencing.

statements.text: The ovarian tumor carried a truncating TP53 mutation, whereas the breast tumor had a PIK3CA hotspot mutation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a truncated mutation in the TP53 gene in the ovarian tumor tissue, and a hotspot mutation in the PIK3CA gene in the breast cancer.
statements.note: The abstract describes exactly these distinct driver mutations in the two tumors.

statements.text: The Phe1695Val variant was shown to impair BRCA1 protein function in a biochemical assay.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: According to our findings, the BRCA1 F1695V mutation is linked to ovarian cancer susceptibility in the family and causes specific somatic mutational profiles.
statements.note: The variant is linked to susceptibility, but no protein-function assay is described.

statements.text: The analysis spanned 14 tumor types from TCGA, with BMI treated as a continuous variable.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A pan-cancer analysis of non-synonymous somatic mutations across 14 tumor types using data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)
statements.note: The abstract describes a 14-tumor-type TCGA analysis with BMI as a continuous variable.

statements.text: Functional analysis indicated gain-of-function mechanisms in most of the top-ranked BLCA genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Functional inactivation analysis suggested loss-of-function mechanisms in most top-ranked genes
statements.note: The analysis suggested loss-of-function, not gain-of-function, mechanisms.

statements.text: Weight loss reduced the mutational burden in bladder cancer patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings support a role for obesity in shaping the genomic landscape of tumors
statements.note: An association with BMI was found, but no weight-loss intervention effect is reported.

statements.text: Bladder urothelial cancer was the tumor most frequently mutated in association with higher BMI.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: bladder urothelial cancer (BLCA) resulted as the most frequently mutated neoplasia in association with higher body mass index.
statements.note: The abstract names BLCA as the most frequently mutated tumor tied to higher BMI.

statements.text: Plasma and urine reached detection sensitivities of 67.6% and 65.6%, while semen was lower at 33.3%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Plasma and urine samples demonstrated high detection sensitivities, reaching 67.6% and 65.6%, respectively, while semen samples showed a lower detection rate of 33.3%.
statements.note: The abstract gives these exact detection sensitivities by sample type.

statements.text: Combining plasma and urine testing raised detection sensitivity above that of tissue.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study validates the utility of urine and plasma samples as non-invasive and sensitive liquid biopsy options for PCa, showing comparable ctDNA detection rates.
statements.note: Plasma and urine were comparable to each other, but a combined-sensitivity figure is not reported and tissue was the 100% gold standard.

statements.text: AR mutations appeared in plasma and semen but were absent from tissue and urine samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: AR mutations were observed with similar frequencies in plasma and semen samples, but were absent in tissue and urine samples.
statements.note: The abstract reports this exact AR-mutation distribution.

statements.text: ctDNA negativity was associated with a significant survival advantage in this cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: No significant survival advantage associated with ctDNA negativity was observed, likely due to the small sample size.
statements.note: No significant survival advantage with ctDNA negativity was found.

statements.text: In the GI cohort, TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene at 51%, ahead of KRAS at 25%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In the GI cohort, TP53 was most frequently mutated (51 %), followed by KRAS (25 %)
statements.note: The abstract reports TP53 at 51% leading the GI cohort, with KRAS at 25%.

statements.text: Among lung cancer patients, TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene at 44%, ahead of EGFR.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Among lung cancer patients, EGFR mutations (44 %), followed by TP53 (43 %)
statements.note: EGFR, not TP53, was the top gene in lung cancer at 44%.

statements.text: Patients with EGFR mutations detected in ctDNA had better responses to targeted therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Study underscores substantial increase in the adoption of liquid biopsy and the real-world utility of ctDNA-based NGS testing in solid tumors contributing to improved patient care management.
statements.note: Adoption and utility are discussed, but no treatment-response outcome tied to mutations is reported.

statements.text: Across 236 ctDNA samples, lung malignancies formed the largest group at 47%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Out of 236 ctDNA samples, majority were lung malignancies (47 %), gastric cancers (43 %)
statements.note: The abstract reports lung malignancies as 47% of the 236 samples.

statements.text: Of 16 somatic mutations found, 12 were in AKT1 and 4 in NRAS.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 16 somatic mutations were identified (12 in AKT1, 4 in NRAS).
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly 12 AKT1 and 4 NRAS somatic mutations.

statements.text: The most common AKT1 mutation was p.Asp32Glu, seen across multiple clinical groups.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most frequent AKT1 mutation was p.Asp32Glu, observed in multiple clinical groups.
statements.note: The abstract names p.Asp32Glu as the most frequent AKT1 mutation.

statements.text: AKT1 mutations were concentrated in early-stage HCC and became rarer in advanced disease.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: AKT1 mutations were more prevalent in intermediate and advanced HCC stages, suggesting a role in tumor progression.
statements.note: AKT1 mutations were more prevalent in intermediate and advanced stages, not early-stage disease.

statements.text: AKT1 inhibitors reduced tumor growth in the treated patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings advocate for expanded molecular profiling in HCC and suggest AKT1 as a promising target for personalized therapy.
statements.note: AKT1 is proposed as a target, but no inhibitor was administered or tested.

statements.text: Against controls, KRAS copy number gain had 16% sensitivity and 100% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The sensitivity and specificity of KRAS CNG compared to the control group were 16% and 100% (AUC-ROC-0.580)
statements.note: The abstract reports 16% sensitivity and 100% specificity for KRAS CNG versus controls.

statements.text: KRAS copy number gain in bile improved post-surgical monitoring of PDAC recurrence.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Bile exhibited an equal KRAS CNG detection rate compared to plasma (20% vs. 16%).
statements.note: A bile detection rate is reported, but its use for post-surgical recurrence monitoring was not studied.

statements.text: Patients with KRAS copy number gain had a better probability of survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The probability of survival was worse in patients with KRAS CNG (HR-3.54; 95% CI: 1.55-8.12; p = 0.001).
statements.note: Survival was worse, not better, in patients with KRAS CNG.

statements.text: Adding KRAS point mutations to the analysis raised sensitivity to 65%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Addition of KRAS point mutations to the analysis increased the sensitivity to 65%
statements.note: The abstract reports sensitivity rising to 65% when point mutations were added.

statements.text: Driver mutations were confined to tumour tissue and were undetectable in phenotypically normal meninges.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: NF2 or TRAF7 driver mutations are detectable in phenotypically normal meninges in 81.8% of cases
statements.note: Driver mutations were in fact detectable in normal meninges in most cases.

statements.text: NF2 or TRAF7 driver mutations were detectable in phenotypically normal meninges in 81.8% of cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: NF2 or TRAF7 driver mutations are detectable in phenotypically normal meninges in 81.8% of cases
statements.note: The abstract gives an 81.8% detection rate in normal meninges.

statements.text: Carriers of these mosaic driver mutations had a higher risk of meningioma recurrence after surgery.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Together, these findings reveal an early origin of human meningioma, in which developmental mosaicism establishes a pre-neoplastic field within the meninges, providing a developmental framework for adult tumourigenesis.
statements.note: The work addresses tumour origin, not post-surgical recurrence risk.

statements.text: The study examined 80 triple-matched tumour, normal meninges, and blood samples from 22 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we analysed 80 triple-matched tumour, histologically normal meninges, and blood samples from 22 patients.
statements.note: The abstract states 80 triple-matched samples from 22 patients.

statements.text: CSF liquid biopsy found frequent mutations in EGFR, BRCA2, and ANKRD11 in BM-LUAD patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: CSF liquid biopsy identified high-frequency mutations in EGFR, BRCA2 , and ANKRD11 among patients with BM-LUAD.
statements.note: The abstract names these three high-frequency mutated genes.

statements.text: Functional assays showed ANKRD11 promotes tumor invasion and metastasis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: in vitro and in vivo assays confirmed its role in suppressing tumor invasion and metastasis.
statements.note: The assays showed ANKRD11 suppresses, not promotes, invasion and metastasis.

statements.text: ANKRD11 expression fell progressively with tumor progression, and assays confirmed it suppresses invasion and metastasis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ScRNA-seq revealed a progressive decrease in ANKRD11 expression along tumor progression, while in vitro and in vivo assays confirmed its role in suppressing tumor invasion and metastasis.
statements.note: The abstract reports both the expression decline and the suppressive role.

statements.text: CSF ctDNA detected brain metastases earlier than MRI in these patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The extensive clinical adoption of liquid biopsy presents a minimally invasive approach for the early detection and treatment management of brain metastasis from lung adenocarcinoma (BM-LUAD).
statements.note: Early detection is the motivation, but no head-to-head timing comparison with MRI is reported.

statements.text: ctDNA-versus-tissue concordance showed 84.8% sensitivity and a 79.4% positive predictive value.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The concordance between intra-patient ctDNA and tumor tissue mutations revealed a sensitivity of 84.8%, and positive predictive value of 79.4%.
statements.note: The abstract gives these concordance metrics.

statements.text: Patients with FGFR2 fusions in ctDNA who received FGFR inhibitors had improved survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA revealed targetable alterations in 34.3% of patients - including FGFR2 fusions, IDH1 mutations, microsatellite instability-high, ERBB2 amplifications, PIK3CA mutations, BRCA1/2 mutations, and MET amplifications.
statements.note: Targetable alterations including FGFR2 fusions were found, but response to matched inhibitors was not assessed.

statements.text: A high maximum somatic variant allele frequency in ctDNA was associated with favorable prognosis after gemcitabine/cisplatin chemotherapy.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A high maximum somatic variant allele frequency in ctDNA was associated with poor prognosis after gemcitabine/cisplatin-based chemotherapy
statements.note: High maximum VAF was tied to poor, not favorable, prognosis.

statements.text: ctDNA identified potentially targetable alterations in 34.3% of the patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA revealed targetable alterations in 34.3% of patients
statements.note: The abstract reports targetable alterations in 34.3% of patients.

statements.text: SigProfilerAssignment is described as the first tool to do both copy-number signature analysis and probabilistic assignment of signatures to individual mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SigProfilerAssignment is the first tool that allows both analysis of copy-number signatures and probabilistic assignment of signatures to individual somatic mutations.
statements.note: The abstract makes this exact claim of being first to combine both capabilities.

statements.text: On 2700 synthetic cancer genomes, it outperformed four commonly used signature-assignment approaches.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of 2700 synthetic cancer genomes with and without noise demonstrates that SigProfilerAssignment outperforms four commonly used approaches for assigning mutational signatures.
statements.note: The abstract reports it outperformed four approaches on 2700 synthetic genomes.

statements.text: SigProfilerAssignment ran faster than the four compared tools.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: As its computational engine, the tool uses a custom implementation of the forward stagewise algorithm for sparse regression and nonnegative least squares for numerical optimization.
statements.note: The engine is described, but runtime or speed versus other tools is not reported.

statements.text: On the 2700 synthetic cancer genomes, SigProfilerAssignment performed worse than four commonly used approaches.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: SigProfilerAssignment outperforms four commonly used approaches for assigning mutational signatures.
statements.note: It outperformed, not underperformed, the four approaches.

statements.text: Post-treatment ctDNA was lower in responders than in nonresponders (2.72 vs 4.18 ng/μL).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Posttreatment ctDNA levels were significantly lower in responders compared with nonresponders (2.72 ± 1.11 vs 4.18 ± 1.54 ng/μL, P < .001).
statements.note: The abstract reports lower post-treatment ctDNA in responders with these values.

statements.text: Post-treatment ctDNA levels were significantly higher in responders than in nonresponders.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Posttreatment ctDNA levels were significantly lower in responders compared with nonresponders (2.72 ± 1.11 vs 4.18 ± 1.54 ng/μL, P < .001).
statements.note: Responders had lower, not higher, post-treatment ctDNA.

statements.text: ctDNA levels predicted overall survival in these advanced NSCLC patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Multivariate Cox regression identified ctDNA levels and treatment modality as independent predictors of PFS.
statements.note: ctDNA predicted progression-free survival; overall survival was not assessed.

statements.text: Low-ctDNA patients had a longer median PFS than high-ctDNA patients (8.6 vs 5.5 months).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: patients with low ctDNA had longer median PFS (8.6 months) than those with high ctDNA (5.5 months, P < .001).
statements.note: The abstract gives these median PFS values by ctDNA level.

statements.text: In C. elegans, an ERI-6/7-dependent siRNA pathway mainly silences retrotransposons and recent genes of likely viral origin.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a small interfering RNA pathway dependent on the helicase ERI-6/7 primarily silences retrotransposons and recent genes of likely viral origin.
statements.note: The abstract describes this silencing role of the ERI-6/7 pathway.

statements.text: Polinton DNA transposon insertions reshuffled the eri-6/7 locus and inverted eri-6 in some wild strains.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: multiple insertions of the DNA transposons, Polintons, reshuffled the eri-6/7 locus and induced inversion of eri-6 in some wild strains.
statements.note: The abstract reports Polinton insertions reshuffling the locus and inverting eri-6.

statements.text: The direct repeats enabling the trans-splicing repair came from retrotransposon LTRs rather than Polinton terminal inverted repeats.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We identified that these direct repeats originated from terminal inverted repeats of Polintons .
statements.note: The direct repeats originated from Polinton terminal inverted repeats, not retrotransposon LTRs.

statements.text: Strains with the inverted eri-6 configuration showed increased susceptibility to viral infection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In the inverted configuration, gene function was previously shown to be repaired by unusual trans-splicing mediated by direct repeats.
statements.note: Gene function was repaired in the inverted configuration; viral-susceptibility consequences were not examined.

statements.text: In the pretreatment setting, tissue-informed ctDNA was detected in 71 of 77 patients (92.2%).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Tissue-informed ctDNA was detected in 71 of 77 patients (92.2%) in the initial pretreatment setting.
statements.note: The abstract gives a 92.2% pretreatment detection rate.

statements.text: Tissue-informed ctDNA detection predicted overall survival in the surveillance cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These metrics support the feasibility of using this assay as a promising ctDNA approach for disease monitoring in HNSCC.
statements.note: The study measured detection accuracy, not survival prediction.

statements.text: In surveillance, the assay reached a per-test sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 100%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the assay demonstrated a per-test sensitivity of 95.2% (20 of 21 patients; 95% CI, 83.3%-100%), specificity of 100%
statements.note: The abstract reports these per-test surveillance metrics.

statements.text: In the surveillance setting the assay's per-test specificity was only about 50%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: specificity of 100% (157 of 157 patients; 95% CI, 100%-100%)
statements.note: Per-test specificity was 100%, not about 50%.

statements.text: TSPY2 formed the highly variable tandem array, while the rest of TSPY was invariable and under strong constraint.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the largest Y-linked gene family TSPY can be divided into a highly variable tandem array whose copy number was found to be associated with prostate cancer risks, and an invariable TSPY2 under stronger functional constraints.
statements.note: It was TSPY2 that was invariable and constrained; the tandem array was the variable part.

statements.text: The copy number of the TSPY tandem array was associated with prostate cancer risk.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the largest Y-linked gene family TSPY can be divided into a highly variable tandem array whose copy number was found to be associated with prostate cancer risks
statements.note: The abstract links TSPY tandem-array copy number to prostate cancer risk.

statements.text: The study analysed Y chromosome sequences from 206 individuals against six ape species, including 160 near-complete East Asian sequences.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: high-quality Y chromosomal sequences of 206 human individuals vs. six ape species, including 160 near complete sequences from the East Asian population, 85 of which are gapless.
statements.note: The abstract gives these sample and comparison numbers.

statements.text: Variation in Yq12 heterochromatin size was associated with a specific disease risk in the cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We uncovered an extensive cryptic diversity of the largest heterochromatin of the human genome on the Y chromosome Yq12, and traced its dual-origin from ancestral centromeric satellites
statements.note: Yq12 diversity and origin were characterized structurally, but no disease association for it is reported.

statements.text: Most free transposable-element transcripts were unchanged in ASD cerebellum compared with unaffected individuals.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The majority of free transcripts of transposable elements were not changed in the cerebellum tissues of ASD compared with unaffected individuals.
statements.note: The abstract states most free TE transcripts were unchanged in ASD.

statements.text: The majority of free transposable-element transcripts were strongly upregulated in ASD cerebellum versus unaffected individuals.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The majority of free transcripts of transposable elements were not changed in the cerebellum tissues of ASD compared with unaffected individuals.
statements.note: Most free TE transcripts were unchanged, not upregulated.

statements.text: Silencing the chimeric transcripts reversed the cerebellar molecular-layer thinning.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: the expression levels of these genes were correlated with the significantly decreased thickness of the molecular layer in the cerebellum of ASD.
statements.note: A correlation with molecular-layer thinning was found, but no silencing experiment testing reversal is reported.

statements.text: LINE-1- and Alu-derived chimeric transcripts were embedded in differentially expressed genes in ASD cerebellum.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: chimeric transcripts derived from LINE-1 and Alu were embedded in the transcripts of differentially expressed genes in the cerebellum of ASD
statements.note: The abstract reports these chimeric transcripts within differentially expressed genes.
